description: Stay with a literary passage at the level of the sentence, the word, the phoneme. Refuse to ascend to theme until the material texture has been inhabited. Use this skill whenever a user shares a passage of literature, poetry, song lyrics, or prose and asks you to analyze it, break it down, examine what it's doing, explain why it works, or reverse-engineer the craft. Also triggers on: 'look at this passage,' 'what is this sentence doing,' 'how does this work,' 'word by word,' 'why does this line hit so hard,' 'close read this,' 'analyze the prose,' 'reverse engineer this writing,' 'break down this paragraph,' or any moment where a specific passage is offered as an object of attention rather than a source of information. If the user shares a literary excerpt and asks a question about craft, technique, style, or effect — use this skill. Do NOT use for academic paper analysis (use paper-hermeneutics), adversarial critique (use paper-scrying), or free-associative riffing (use paper-riffing).
